method: Adversarial verification of the round-4 fix commit (A1-A4) plus a whole-plan coherence sweep across proposal.md, both spec deltas, design.md, tasks.md, and work-packages.yaml. Every finding below is backed by a command run in the worktree; the command and its output are quoted in the description. Round-4 findings preserved verbatim at reviews/review-findings-plan-r4.json. reviews/consensus-plan.json was not consulted (round-1 lexical-similarity artifact). openspec validate --strict and validate_work_packages.py were both run and are both green; per issue #324 that was treated as no evidence either way.
verification_log: A1: `sed -n '1,40p' .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> THREE triggers: `push: branches: [main]`, `pull_request:`, `merge_group:`. The spec names bases for two.
A1: `grep -n 'if:' .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> the only hit is `if: failure()` (line 451). NO job in ci.yml is guarded by `github.event_name`; every job runs on all three triggers.
A1: `grep -rn 'event_name' <all plan artifacts>` -> zero hits. The plan names base EXPRESSIONS but never the discriminator that selects between them or the events the job runs on.
A2: spec.md:517-535 + scenarios `non-openspec-pr-skips` (594-601) and `unresolvable-base-fails-not-skips` (603-612) -> the SKIP/ERROR distinction IS in the spec delta, not only design.md. A2 passes.
A3: `grep -n '\*\*Spec scenarios\*\*' tasks.md` -> task 5.7 (line 594) enumerates 4 scenarios and omits `unresolvable-base-fails-not-skips`; it survives only in prose Notes at 616-627.
A3: wp-wiring write_allow covers `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `skills/tests/validate-feature/**`, `skills/pyproject.toml` -> the CI work has an owner with the right scope. A3 partially passes.

A4: on the unmodified tree, `test -f openspec/contracts/gen-eval-framework/traceability-exclusions.yaml && grep -q traceability: ...` -> exit 1 (fails, good); `test -f skills/tests/validate-feature/test_ci_sweep_wiring.py` -> exit 1 (fails, good); `grep -q '"tests/validate-feature"' skills/pyproject.toml` -> exit 1 (fails, good); `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests/validate-feature -q` -> 5 passed, exit 0 (does NOT fail before the work).

Coherence: `grep -n '\[human\]' tasks.md` -> SEVEN tagged tasks (4.1, 4.2, 4.2b, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.7c), and the work-packages carve-out comment names exactly those seven plus 4.3 with a stated reason. The exclusion list matches the tags. No unowned-by-accident task found.
Coherence: `npx @fission-ai/openspec validate trace-requirements-to-contracts --strict` -> valid. `validate_work_packages.py` -> VALID (schema, depends_on_refs, dag_cycles, lock_keys).

Coherence: SKIP paths do not collide - the validate-feature gate-absent SKIP (skill-workflow delta, different process) and the CI no-change-directory SKIP (gen-eval delta) share no code path, and the change-scope `unresolvable-scope-errors` rule is correctly scoped to change-scoped runs only, so it does not make the capability-scope post-merge run (which legitimately omits --change) an error.

findings.title: The round-4 fix names the base per event but never says which events the blocking JOB runs on - and ci.yml has three triggers, none of its jobs event-guarded
findings.description:
This is the third consecutive round in which the fix for the previous round's finding introduces a new fail-open one level up. Round 4 correctly named the base per event. It did not say how the job knows which event it is on, or which events it runs on at all - and that is now the load-bearing gap.

EVIDENCE.
(a) `sed -n '1,40p' .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows THREE triggers, not two:
    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      pull_request:
      merge_group:
(b) `grep -n 'if:' .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns exactly one hit, `if: failure()` at line 451. NOT ONE of the eleven jobs in ci.yml is guarded on `github.event_name`. The repository's established pattern is an unconditional job that runs on all three triggers. The nearest analogue, `context-drift-gate` (ci.yml:114-140), diffs `main...HEAD` unconditionally - on a push to `main` that diff is empty and the gate validates nothing while exiting zero, which is this exact defect already living in the file the new job will be copied from.
(c) `grep -rn 'event_name' <all five plan artifacts>` returns ZERO hits. The plan names `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` and `github.event.merge_group.base_sha` but never the discriminator that selects between them, and never states an event condition on the job.
(d) wp-wiring's `write_allow` (work-packages.yaml:481) contains `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and no other workflow path, so the package CANNOT create a separate workflow file with a narrower `on:` block - a scope check would reject it. The job MUST go into ci.yml, which triggers on all three events. The event guard therefore has to be a job-level `if:`, and nothing in the plan asks for one.

CONSEQUENCE. The implementer has to invent the guard, and the plan's own wording pushes toward the wrong one. Three artifacts say the blocking sweep is `pull_request`-triggered and say nothing about merge_group as a trigger:
  - design.md:412, the D12 table: `| CI full sweep | `pull_request` | ... |`
  - tasks.md:634: 'the BLOCKING sweep is `pull_request`-triggered.'
  - work-packages.yaml:408: 'wire the full-capability sweep into ci.yml as a `pull_request` job'
Two implementations follow, both defective:
  (i) `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` - the literal reading of wp-wiring's dispatch text. The blocking job then never runs on `merge_group`. The whole round-4 fix - merge_group base derivation, the unresolvable-base ERROR, the new scenario - becomes unreachable code, and the merge queue is unevaluated by the blocking sweep at the one moment it is the last check standing. That is round 4's finding restated: not a silent skip this time, an absent job. Depending on branch-protection configuration a required check that does not run on merge_group is either reported green or leaves the group hanging; in neither case does the sweep evaluate anything.
  (ii) No `if:` at all - the repo's actual convention per (b). The job then runs on `push: branches: [main]`, where NEITHER named base exists, and spec.md:520 makes that a hard failure ('Where that base cannot be resolved, the job SHALL fail naming the event'). CI reds on every push to main from the day this lands. Round 4 converted a fail-open into a fail-closed without bounding which events it closes on.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE. State the event set normatively, in the spec delta (the artifact that survives archive), not only in design.md: the blocking job SHALL run on `pull_request` and `merge_group` and SHALL NOT run on `push`; the base SHALL be selected on `github.event_name`; an event that reaches the blocking job with no base rule is the unresolvable-base ERROR. Correct D12's trigger column to name both events, correct tasks.md:634 and work-packages.yaml:408 which currently say `pull_request` only, and add the event condition to the scenario `unresolvable-base-fails-not-skips` so the test written for it exercises a reachable path.

findings.title: On merge_group the diff spans every PR in the group, so the 'two change directories = ambiguous, fail' rule fails the merge queue whenever two OpenSpec changes batch
findings.description:
The round-4 fix extended the change-id derivation to `merge_group` without revisiting the ambiguity rule written for a single pull request, and the two clauses now sit in the same paragraph contradicting each other operationally.

spec.md:517-524 says the blocking job derives its change id from 'the change directory under `openspec/changes/` touched by the diff against a named base: ... the merge group's base commit on a `merge_group` event', and 'Where it touches more than one, the job SHALL fail as ambiguous rather than choosing.' Scenario `ambiguous-change-fails` (spec.md:614-620) repeats it.

A merge group's base_sha is the commit the GROUP is based on and its head is the temporary commit containing EVERY pull request queued in that group. `git diff <merge_group.base_sha>...HEAD` therefore spans all of them. GitHub batches multiple pull requests per group by default. The moment two OpenSpec changes are queued together - the normal case for this repository, which runs an agent-driven multi-PR workflow - the diff touches two directories under `openspec/changes/` and the blocking job SHALL fail as ambiguous, ejecting both pull requests from the queue. They re-queue and can batch again.

This is not a hypothetical reachability argument: it is reachable under exactly the same premise round 4 used to justify the fix ('`merge_group` ... triggered unfiltered by this repository's CI', spec.md:531-532). If merge_group is reachable enough to justify a new SHALL, it is reachable enough to batch.

Nothing in spec.md, design.md D12, tasks.md 5.7, or wp-wiring's description mentions this. `grep -rn 'merge_group|merge queue' <all plan artifacts>` returns 13 hits, every one of them about the BASE, none about the multi-change diff.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE. The ambiguity rule needs to be event-aware. On `pull_request`, two touched change directories is a genuine ambiguity and should fail. On `merge_group`, two touched directories is the expected shape of a batched queue and must not fail - the honest options are to evaluate each touched change in turn and fail if ANY fails (which preserves the gate's purpose and is a small change to 3.16's already-existing per-change resolution), or to state normatively that the blocking job is not enqueued for merge_group and accept that the pull_request run is the last check - but that second option contradicts finding 1's requirement and the round-4 rationale, so it is not really available. Whichever is chosen, say it in the spec delta and give scenario `ambiguous-change-fails` an explicit `pull_request` precondition so it does not read as universal.

findings.title: proposal.md still describes the pre-round-3 CI model - it says the integration-branch sweep BLOCKS, contradicting D12, the spec delta, and itself
findings.description:
This is the round-2/3/4 defect shape (the fix does not propagate to the artifact that owns the consequence) sitting in the change's top-level artifact, which nobody has re-read since round 1.

Round 3 moved the blocking sweep off `push`-on-`main` and onto the merge candidate. design.md:415-423 states the correction at length ('a push event on `main` fires **after** the merge has landed ... It can red `main`; it cannot stop `main` going red'), and spec.md:501-506 encodes it ('SHALL run as a blocking check on the merge candidate, and SHALL run again, explicitly non-blocking, on the integration branch after merge'). proposal.md was never updated and still asserts the model that was rejected:

  - proposal.md:64-68: 'Two run contexts, one gate. At `/validate-feature` it is scoped to what the change touches and blocks. On the integration branch it sweeps every capability: opted-in surfaces block, the rest report.'  There are now THREE run contexts, and the integration-branch one is precisely the one that must NOT block.
  - proposal.md:229-230, in the Acceptance Outcomes list: 'The full sweep on the integration branch fails on violations in opted-in surfaces and reports the rest.'  This is an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION requiring the post-merge job to fail - the exact thing D12 forbids ('explicitly non-blocking, so nothing depends on it to stop anything').
  - proposal.md:251, in the risks table, has the corrected version: 'The integration-branch sweep (D12) reports them in full without blocking.'

So proposal.md contradicts the spec delta, contradicts the operator-settled D12, and contradicts itself between line 229 and line 251. All of it passes `openspec validate --strict` (verified: 'Change ... is valid'), which is issue #324 exactly.

Why this is blocking rather than cosmetic: an implementer wiring the two CI jobs who reads the Acceptance Outcomes list - the natural place to look for 'when is this done' - is told to make the push-on-main job fail. That reintroduces the after-the-fact blocking check D12 was rewritten to remove, and it does so via an artifact no validator checks.

Secondary, same list: the Acceptance Outcomes have an outcome for the change-scope unresolvable merge base (line 227) but none for the round-4 unresolvable-base failure in CI. Add one.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE. Rewrite proposal.md:64-68 to name three run contexts (validation / blocking merge-candidate sweep / non-blocking post-merge sweep), rewrite the acceptance outcome at 229-230 so the blocking claim attaches to the merge candidate and the integration-branch run is stated as reporting-only, and add an acceptance outcome for the unresolvable-base ERROR.

findings.title: The skill-workflow delta forbids hand-filling Contract Ref, but the file that instructs the hand-fill is owned by no task and writable by no package
findings.description:
This is the 'a scenario with no owner is work that will silently not happen' check, and it fails on a SHALL NOT in the spec delta.

skill-workflow spec delta, scenario 'Phase 1 - Test plan (pre-implementation)' (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:14): '**AND** Contract Ref SHALL NOT be populated by hand when the capability has any traced contract document.'

`grep -rln 'Contract Ref' skills/ docs/` returns exactly three files:
  1. skills/plan-feature/install_assets/openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/change-context.md
  2. skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md
  3. docs/parallel-agentic-development.md

Only #2 is covered. wp-matrix's `write_allow` is `packages/gen-eval/scripts/generate_contract_refs.py`, `packages/gen-eval/tests/test_contract_ref_generation.py`, `skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md` (work-packages.yaml:361-364). Task 5.5's note (tasks.md:568-570) names `skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md` and nothing else. D8 (design.md:263-289) names `skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md` and nothing else. proposal.md's in-scope list (line 94) names `skills/implement-feature/` and NOT `skills/plan-feature/`. `grep -n '^        - "' work-packages.yaml` confirms no package's write_allow contains any `skills/plan-feature/` path.

File #1 is the template that carries the hand-fill instruction and it is the PRIMARY one - it is what becomes each change's `change-context.md`. Lines 13-15 read: 'Phase 1: Fill Req ID, Spec Source, Description, Contract Ref, Design Decision, Test(s).  Contract Ref: path to contract file the requirement maps to (e.g., contracts/openapi/v1.yaml#/paths/~1users), or "---" if no contract applies.' That is an instruction to populate the column by hand, and `grep -n 'install_assets' skills/install.sh` (line 369) confirms `<skill>/install_assets/openspec` is rsynced into every consumer repository, so the contradicting instruction ships downstream too.

This is the known failure mode 'write_allow misses invalidated files - scope is drawn around files you edit, not files your edit invalidates', and it is the same shape as findings in rounds 2, 3, and 4. The consequence if it ships: the generator exists, the spec forbids hand-filling, and every future change scaffolded from the template is still told to hand-fill - the unenforced-convention problem D8 says this change exists to fix, surviving in the file that states the convention. An agent running wp-matrix that DOES notice hits a scope violation and cannot fix it.

Secondary: tasks 5.4 and 5.5 carry no `**Spec scenarios**` line at all (tasks.md:556-570), so the skill-workflow MODIFIED scenario that added these SHALL/SHALL NOT clauses maps to no task by the plan's own convention (skills/plan-feature/SKILL.md:423: 'Every SHALL/MUST scenario in specs must be covered by at least one test task').

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE. Add `skills/plan-feature/install_assets/openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/change-context.md` to wp-matrix's `write_allow` and name it in task 5.5's note alongside implement-feature/SKILL.md; add `skills/plan-feature/` to proposal.md's in-scope list; decide explicitly whether `docs/parallel-agentic-development.md:186` is updated in this change or left as known drift, and say which. Add `**Spec scenarios**` lines to 5.4 and 5.5.

findings.title: The round-4 scenario `unresolvable-base-fails-not-skips` appears in no task's Spec scenarios mapping - it survives only in prose
findings.description:
`grep -n '\*\*Spec scenarios\*\*' tasks.md` shows task 5.7's mapping line enumerates four scenarios of the requirement 'The full sweep blocks opted-in surfaces and reports the rest': (an opted-in surface fails the sweep); (a surface that has not opted in is reported, not failed); (a pull request that was not planned through OpenSpec skips); (a diff touching two change directories fails as ambiguous). The fifth CI-side scenario added by 14a6c839, 'An unresolvable base fails rather than skipping' (spec.md:603-612), is absent from that line and from every other task's mapping line - the requirement's other two scenarios are correctly mapped to 3.16 (tasks.md:433), so this is not a systematic omission, it is the new one specifically.

It is not lost - three Notes under 5.7 (tasks.md:616-627) describe the behavior and mandate 'assert BOTH paths in the wiring tests'. So the implementer will most likely build it, which is why this is a nit and not a blocker. But the mapping line is the mechanical statement of which task owns which scenario, it is the convention plan-feature states as a rule (SKILL.md:423), and 'the fix landed everywhere except the artifact that declares ownership' is precisely the propagation defect rounds 2, 3, and 4 each found. One line.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE. Append '(an unresolvable base fails rather than skipping)' to task 5.7's Spec scenarios line.

findings.title: `test -f test_ci_sweep_wiring.py` is satisfied by `touch` - and the companion pytest step passes on an empty file too, so neither CI scenario has a verification that can fail
findings.description:
The paired nit fixed in 14a6c839 added this verification step to wp-wiring:

  - name: "the CI-sweep wiring scenarios have a test that exists"
    command: "test -f skills/tests/validate-feature/test_ci_sweep_wiring.py"

Judged on its own it asserts existence and says nothing about contents. The question is whether the surrounding steps close that. They do not, and I checked rather than inferred. On the unmodified tree:
  `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests/validate-feature -q` -> '5 passed', exit 0.
That step therefore passes TODAY, before any of this work exists - it is a regression guard, not a coverage guard, and it will keep passing if `test_ci_sweep_wiring.py` is created empty (pytest collects zero tests from it and the suite still exits zero on the five pre-existing ones). So `touch skills/tests/validate-feature/test_ci_sweep_wiring.py` satisfies both steps, and tasks.md:631-633 says these two scenarios are 'the only ones in the change with no mechanism that notices they were never written'. The mechanism is currently defeatable by `touch`.

Credit where due, three of the four wp-wiring steps DO fail on the unmodified tree, which is the right shape: the human-precondition step exits 1, the `test -f` step exits 1, and `grep -q '"tests/validate-feature"' skills/pyproject.toml` exits 1 (confirmed: testpaths at skills/pyproject.toml:52-100 lists tests/implement-feature and tests/plan-feature but not tests/validate-feature, so task 5.7b's premise is verified true).

WHAT WOULD BE ADEQUATE. Replace the presence assertion with a collection assertion that names the two behaviors, e.g. a step that runs `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests/validate-feature/test_ci_sweep_wiring.py --collect-only -q` and requires a non-zero test count, paired with a `grep -q 'merge_group' skills/tests/validate-feature/test_ci_sweep_wiring.py` and a grep for the SKIP assertion - two greps for the two paths the task's own note demands. An empty file then fails all three. Note this interacts with finding 1: if the blocking job ends up `pull_request`-only, the unresolvable-base test will be asserting behavior on a path the job never takes, and a content assertion is what would surface that.

findings.title: Verification results that came back clean
findings.description:
Recorded so the next round does not re-litigate them.

A2 PASSES. The SKIP/ERROR distinction lives in the spec delta, not only in design.md. spec.md:526-535 states it as requirement prose ('An unresolvable base and an absent change directory SHALL NOT share an exit path. They are opposite conditions...'), and two separate scenarios encode the two exits: `non-openspec-pr-skips` (594-601, precondition 'whose base resolves and whose diff touches no directory') and `unresolvable-base-fails-not-skips` (603-612). An implementer reading only specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md learns both. The round-4 fix genuinely shipped in the artifact that survives archive.

A3 PARTIALLY PASSES. The CI work has an owner with adequate scope: wp-wiring's write_allow includes `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `skills/tests/validate-feature/**`, and `skills/pyproject.toml`, so per-event base derivation and a distinct failure path are writable by the package that must build them. The gaps are the mapping line (finding 5) and the strength of the verification (finding 6), not ownership.

The [human] carve-out is CORRECT and COMPLETE. `grep -n '\[human\]' tasks.md` returns seven tagged tasks: 4.1, 4.2, 4.2b, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.7c. The work-packages carve-out comment (work-packages.yaml:546-565) names exactly those seven, and separately excludes 4.3 with a stated reason ('its whole value is that a person watches the real gate fail on the real contract') - 4.3 is scripted verification, not judgement work, so it is correctly untagged, and tasks.md:465-467 says so. Package coverage is 1.1-1.5 / 2.0-2.5 / 3.1-3.16 / 5.4-5.5 / 5.6-5.9-except-5.7c; all of phase 4 is deliberately unowned. No task falls through.

The three SKIP paths do not collide. The validate-feature gate-absent SKIP and the CI no-change-directory SKIP live in different processes and share no code path; task 5.6's consumer-repo SKIP IS the skill-workflow gate-absent SKIP, not a third one. The change-scope `unresolvable-scope-errors` rule is correctly scoped to change-scoped runs, so it does not make the post-merge capability-scope run (which legitimately omits --change) an error - tasks.md:451-453 states that trap explicitly and avoids it.

Both validators are green: `npx @fission-ai/openspec validate trace-requirements-to-contracts --strict` -> 'Change is valid'; `validate_work_packages.py` -> VALID (schema, depends_on_refs, dag_cycles, lock_keys). Per issue #324 this was treated as no evidence - findings 1, 2, 3, and 4 all survive both.
